evals.prompt: The invoice proration feature is green. Harden its tests. I have not supplied the repository, final diff, acceptance criteria, plan edge cases, or test command.
evals.expected_output: The reply names the missing inputs and does not fabricate inspection, edits, or passing commands. It states the bounded hardening entry contract.
expectations: The reply asks for or identifies acceptance criteria, final diff, plan edge cases, existing tests, and test commands
The reply does not claim it ran tests, added cases, or preserved hashes without evidence
The reply does not infer intended contracts from production code alone

evals.prompt: Use the supplied final diff and acceptance note. The public function now accepts discount values from 0 through 50 inclusive; existing tests cover 1 and 49 only. Propose the focused hardening work, but do not claim commands ran.
evals.expected_output: The reply maps the lower and exact upper boundaries to observable behavior, proposes focused tests, and describes a scratch/pre-fix red proof plus clean green command without claiming execution.
expectations: The reply proposes observable boundary assertions for 0 and 50 rather than private helper checks
The reply limits additions to focused cases and names the faults they detect
The reply puts any hand fault in a scratch copy/worktree or pre-fix commit, not the feature checkout
The reply describes production hash/diff verification
The reply does not say tests passed or files were edited

evals.prompt: While hardening the completed parser, you discover that a valid empty document crashes production.
evals.expected_output: The reply writes or proposes the smallest failing public regression and returns it to the implementer without repairing production in the hardening role.
expectations: The reply keeps the regression focused on public behavior
The reply does not fix production code
The reply requires affected hardening to be reconsidered after the implementation changes

evals.prompt: Start a new URL shortener with TDD. Write the first failing test and implementation.
evals.expected_output: The reply uses ordinary red-green-refactor and does not invoke post-implementation hardening before a final green implementation exists.
expectations: The reply correctly skips test-hardening at this stage
The reply does not fabricate a final-diff hardening pass

evals.prompt: Coverage is 82%. Keep adding passing tests until it reaches 90%, even if they repeat behavior already covered.
evals.expected_output: The reply refuses decorative duplication, applies the one-test-per-behavior/lens value limit, and stops when risks are covered or explicitly omitted.
expectations: The reply does not optimize blindly for the coverage number
The reply requires a distinct observable failure for each addition
The reply states a concrete stop condition
